unit_title: School Life & The World Around Us
curriculum_standards: DEPPS-APS: Communicating everyday school routines, emotional states, healthy lifestyle habits, and global customs in English
CEFR A1: Can describe daily routines, understand school canteen menus and party invitations, express frequency with adverbs, and compare international breakfast traditions

stories.title: West Wimbledon's School Newspaper
stories.summary: Mark's school newspaper features Nadine's Eurodisney trip email, the canteen menu with prices, and the Halloween party invitation.
stories.narrative: Mark attends West Wimbledon Primary School in London. Today, pupils read the new edition of the school newspaper. In the first column, Nadine sends an excited email from Marseilles about her upcoming school trip to Eurodisney by high-speed TGV train. She is sad because her best friend is ill and cannot come. On the right, the school canteen publishes its autumn menu: muffins and apple pie for seventy pence, croissants and doughnuts for fifty pence, and cold bottled water for thirty pence. At the bottom, the headmistress Mrs Clark invites all parents and children to the annual Halloween party on Tuesday October 31st in the school playground.
stories.book_check: Pupil's Book pp. 26-27: West Wimbledon's school newspaper with email, canteen menu, and party invitation.

stories.title: Classroom & School Life at West Wimbledon
stories.summary: Pupils travel on the school bus, borrow books in the library, study in the classroom, and talk about their feelings.
stories.narrative: School life at West Wimbledon is lively and full of activity every weekday. In the morning, pupils ride the yellow school bus to school. On the bus, children experience different feelings: some pupils are happy and excited to see their friends, while others feel tired after waking up early. At nine o'clock, morning classes begin in the classroom where teachers explain history and geography. At break time, pupils run to the library to borrow exciting books, or gather in the playground for games. Mark loves visiting the computer lab to work on his class project.

stories.title: Interview with a Star Athlete — Habits & Health
stories.summary: A famous basketball player visits school to share his daily routines, training schedule, and good health habits.
stories.narrative: Today a famous professional basketball player visits the school gym for an exclusive interview with pupils. The teacher and class welcome their special guest. When asked how he became so successful, the athlete explains that he maintains strict good habits. He sleeps well for eight hours every night and eats a healthy balanced diet with fresh fruit, vegetables, and milk. He trains for six hours each day with his coach to keep fit and practise his shooting. He advises the pupils that regular exercise, drinking plenty of water, and avoiding junk food are essential for every young person.

stories.title: Customs & Breakfasts Around the World
stories.summary: Pupils discover how people around the world start their mornings, what they eat for breakfast, and polite manners.
stories.narrative: In Lesson 3, pupils explore cultural traditions and breakfast customs across different countries. In the United Kingdom, a traditional morning breakfast features fried eggs, bacon, hot buttered toast, and black tea with milk. In Japan, families eat a hot nutritious meal of steamed rice, fish, and miso soup using wooden chopsticks. Japanese pupils politely bow to greet their teachers and always take off shoes before stepping into a home. In Greece, children enjoy fresh bread with honey, cereal with cold milk, and orange juice. Understanding these customs teaches everyone good manners and intercultural respect.

grammar_lab.title: Grammar Lab: Adverbs of Frequency & Daily Routines
target_structures: Adverbs of Frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never)
Word order: before main verbs, after verb 'to be'
Prepositions of Time: in, on, at

frequency_spectrum.example: I always do my homework before dinner.
He usually walks to primary school on foot.
We often play basketball in the playground.
I sometimes buy a muffin at the canteen.
She rarely drinks sugary soft drinks.
They never arrive late for their lessons.

rules.usage: Place adverbs of frequency BEFORE main verbs, but AFTER the verb 'to be'.
examples: Kostas usually arrives on time. (Before main verb: arrives)
Mark is always happy at school. (After verb 'to be': is)

rules.usage: In the Present Simple, add -s or -es to the verb with he, she, or it.
examples: He wakes up at seven in the morning.
She finishes classes at two o'clock.

rules.usage: Use 'in' for parts of the day and months; 'on' for days and dates; 'at' for precise times and night.
examples: We study maths in the morning.
We have gym lessons on Tuesdays.
The Halloween party starts at 6:00 pm.

practice_items.sentence: The star athlete _____ (always / sleep) eight hours every night.
practice_items.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go BEFORE main verbs, with -s for 3rd person singular: always sleeps.

practice_items.sentence: Mark is _____ (never / late) for his morning classes.
practice_items.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go AFTER the verb 'to be' (is): is never late.

practice_items.sentence: How _____ do you practise basketball each week?
practice_items.explanation: We use the question phrase 'How often...?' to ask about the frequency of a habit.
For 3rd person singular (Nadine = she), the negative form is 'doesn't eat'.

practice_items.sentence: The school Halloween party takes place _____ October 31st.
practice_items.explanation: We use the preposition 'on' with specific dates: on October 31st.

practice_items.sentence: Henry _____ (wake) up at seven in the boarding school dormitory.
practice_items.explanation: For he/she/it in the Present Simple, we add -s: Henry wakes up.

authentic_listening.title: Interview with a Famous Sports Star

dialogue_script.speaker: Teacher
dialogue_script.text: We are very happy to have such a famous basketball player here today!

dialogue_script.speaker: Guest
dialogue_script.text: Thank you! I am really happy to be here with your class.

dialogue_script.speaker: Teacher
dialogue_script.text: How did you become so successful and famous in sports?

dialogue_script.speaker: Guest
dialogue_script.text: I practise a lot. I sleep well, and I eat healthily every day. My family is always behind me.

dialogue_script.speaker: Teacher
dialogue_script.text: How many hours do you practise each day?

dialogue_script.speaker: Guest
dialogue_script.text: About six hours, plus I train to stay fit.

dialogue_script.speaker: Teacher
dialogue_script.text: Is the food you eat important?

dialogue_script.speaker: Guest
dialogue_script.text: Yes, it is very important for a basketball player to eat well, like any professional athlete.

true_false_quiz.statement: The guest athlete sleeps well and eats healthily every day.
true_false_quiz.explanation: True. The athlete says: 'I sleep well, and I eat healthily every day.'

true_false_quiz.statement: The athlete only practises for one hour each week.
true_false_quiz.explanation: False. The athlete practises for about six hours each day to stay fit.

true_false_quiz.statement: Healthy nutrition is important for professional sports players.
true_false_quiz.explanation: True. The guest states eating well is very important for an athlete.

true_false_quiz.statement: The basketball star never trains with his family or coach.
true_false_quiz.explanation: False. The player says his family is always behind him and supports his training.

content_true_false.fact: A chocolate muffin costs seventy pence (70p) at West Wimbledon school canteen.
content_true_false.explanation: True. The canteen price list shows muffins for 70p.

content_true_false.fact: Nadine takes a high-speed TGV train from Marseilles to Eurodisney.
content_true_false.explanation: True. Nadine writes in her email that her class travels by TGV straight from Marseilles.

content_true_false.fact: In Japan, people traditionally eat rice with metal forks and knives.
content_true_false.explanation: False. People in Japan traditionally eat rice using wooden chopsticks.

content_true_false.fact: Professional athletes usually eat junk food and stay up late every night.
content_true_false.explanation: False. Athletes follow good habits: they sleep well, train hard, and eat nutritious meals.

content_true_false.fact: Adverbs of frequency like 'always' are placed after the verb 'to be'.
content_true_false.explanation: True. In English grammar, we place adverbs of frequency after the verb to be (e.g. He is always on time).

writing_workshop.default_topic: A Typical School Day & Healthy Habits

paragraphs.heading: Morning Routine & Going to School
paragraphs.guiding_questions: What time do you wake up? What do you eat for breakfast? How do you go to school?
paragraphs.sample_starter: I usually wake up at seven o'clock in the morning. For breakfast, I have cereal with milk and a glass of orange juice. Then I catch the school bus.

paragraphs.heading: Classes, Lessons & Favourite Subjects
paragraphs.guiding_questions: When do lessons start? What subjects do you have? Which subject is your favourite?
paragraphs.sample_starter: Lessons start at eight-fifteen in the classroom. We study English, maths, science, and history. My favourite subject is English because I love writing to pen-pals.

paragraphs.heading: Break Time & School Canteen
paragraphs.guiding_questions: What do you do during break? Where do you go? What snacks do you like?
paragraphs.sample_starter: At break time, I play with my classmates in the school playground. When I feel hungry, I go to the school canteen and buy an apple or a warm muffin.

paragraphs.heading: After School, Training & Good Habits
paragraphs.guiding_questions: When do classes finish? Do you do sports or homework? What good habits do you have?
paragraphs.sample_starter: In the afternoon, classes finish at two o'clock. I always do my homework first, and then I practise basketball with my team to keep fit and strong.
